# dsh-image-edge-cap

Limits the **images sent to the providers or models you choose** in DeepSeek
Harness (DSH): the **lo

ngest side** of each image, and the **number of images**
per request. It has its own page in the **P

f each image, and the **number of images**
per request. It has its own page in the **Plugins** view.

- **Source code:** github.com/mrbeandev/dsh-image-edge-cap
- **npm package:** npmjs.com/package/dsh-

e:** github.com/mrbeandev/dsh-image-edge-cap
- **npm package:** npmjs.com/package/dsh-image-edge-cap

Only the copy sent in the model request changes. Stored attachments and
session logs never change, a

nd providers or models without limits get
exactly the same requests as before.

## Supported DSH versions

## Why this plugin exists

DSH resends the whole conversation, including every image so far, with each
model request. Some prov

iders reject a request once its images cross a limit.
From then on every turn fails: retries, `conti

nue`, and `/compact` all resend
the same images.

**Image too large (Anthropic).** A request with **more than 20 images** is
rejected when any image i
s **over 2000 px on either side**:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

DSH's `requestImagePixelBudget` limits **total pixels** (width × height), not
side length. Tall or w

ide images therefore pass it unchanged: a full-page
mobile screenshot of 390 × 2475 is only 0.97 MP.
**Max edge = 2000** sends it as 315 × 2000.

**Too many images (Cloudflare Workers AI).** Workers AI rejects a request with
more than **32 distin

ct images**. DSH's OpenAI client shows this as
`400 status code (no body)`, because Cloudflare puts
the reason under `errors`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

DSH can drop old images, but only when its adapter raises a byte-limit error,
which this plain 400 i

s not. **Max images = 32** keeps the newest 32 distinct
images in every request. Older ones are sent

as DSH's own short text note
(`[image omitted to fit request image limits; …]`), so the session con

's own short text note
(`[image omitted to fit request image limits; …]`), so the session continues.

Both cases were reproduced and fixed against the real services. Through the
real DSH runtime, 33 dis

tinct screenshots to `@cf/deepseek-ai/…` returned the
400 without the plugin and succeeded with **Ma

x images = 32**; 32 images
succeeded either way.
## How it works
**Max edge**

1. An `llm/stream` listener reads the request's `provider` and `model`. If no
edge limit applies, it

returns the stream untouched.
2. Otherwise it runs the adapter stream inside an `AsyncLocalStorage`

scope
that holds the limit. The scope reaches the image reads the adapter makes
while the stream is

consumed, even through other `llm/stream` listeners and
concurrent requests.
3. The plugin wraps `r

eadImageRequest` on the `attachments` service. Inside a
limited scope it lowers the requested target

so the long edge fits, with
the short edge rounded the same way the store resizes.
4. The attachmen

t store resizes the image with its own code and caches it
under a new variant id. The plugin contain

the image with its own code and caches it
under a new variant id. The plugin contains no image code.
**Max images**

1. The plugin wraps the LLM runtime's `forAdapter` step, the last step before
a request reaches the

provider adapter. Plain calls, prepared agent calls,
retries and compaction summaries all pass throu

gh it.
2. It counts the request's **distinct** images, by attachment, at each image's
newest positio

n. A screenshot resent five times counts once, as with
Cloudflare's limit.
3. When there are more th

an *N*, it marks the older ones `offloaded` on the
request copy only. That is the same mark DSH's ow

n image-offload plugin
uses, so every adapter already sends DSH's placeholder text for them.

Each change is logged once per process, for example
`dsh-image-edge-cap: capped a request image 390×

2475 → 315×2000 (max edge 2000)` and
`dsh-image-edge-cap: sent the newest 32 of 33 images to cf-work

0 (max edge 2000)` and
`dsh-image-edge-cap: sent the newest 32 of 33 images to cf-workers-ai/@cf/…`.
## Compatibility and risk

The plugin wraps two internal methods, both reversibly:
`attachments.readImageRequest` and `llm.forA

dapter`. Neither is an official
extension API. Each wrapper is installed when its service appears, r

emoved
when the plugin is disposed, and never installed twice. The version gate
refuses DSH releases

outside the tested range. If `forAdapter` is ever
missing, the plugin logs a warning and keeps only

ted range. If `forAdapter` is ever
missing, the plugin logs a warning and keeps only the edge limit.

- Both limits apply to any adapter that prepares request images through these
seams. On DSH 0.2 that

is the **pi-ai** adapter (custom OpenAI-compatible,
Anthropic, Cloudflare and other pi-ai providers

does DSH's own pixel, byte or image
budgets; it can only send fewer or smaller images.
- **Dropped i

mages are not seen by the model** on that request, as with DSH's
own image offload. Set Max images j
ust under the provider's real limit.
Plugin config keys (on the `dsh-image-edge-cap` entry):
| Key | Meaning |

| `limits` | Per-provider, per-model limits edited by the plugin page. |
| `providers` | 0.1.x per-p

rovider rules; still honoured until the provider is saved. |
| `enabled: false` | Load without limit

ing anything. |
| `harnessEntry` | Path of the running dsh CLI entry (detected automatically). |
| `
allowUntestedHarness: true` | Load on a DSH outside the supported range. Not recommended. |
